speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help assess your situation, could you please tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and when the bleeding started?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and history of prior cesarean section, I am highly concerned for uterine rupture. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Abdomen and Pelvis: Findings suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Gastroenteritis would not cause vaginal bleeding or a prior cesarean scar to become symptomatic in this manner; your presentation is classic for uterine rupture. REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Heart_Rate_Monitoring

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring: Shows recurrent variable decelerations

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of recurrent variable decelerations, severe abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and a prior cesarean section strongly indicates uterine rupture. I must immediately prepare for an emergency cesarean delivery to save both you and the baby. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
